purpose: Provide a session-bounded, evaluable ontology of concrete market-research and marketing-analytics work units (research methods, customer insight, marketing metrics, and experimentation) so a knowledge searcher can locate, sequence, validate, and synthesize authoritative methods for finding and using market knowledge.
assumptions: no observed dataset, logs, or benchmark evidence supplied; all values are heuristic priors
domain is a subdomain of marketing_and_growth scoped to research methods, customer insight, marketing metrics, and experimentation
statistical inference is composed from a separate statistics specialist rather than re-derived here
nodes are concrete research/analytics work units bounded to one heavy reasoning session
exclusions: creative and media execution, brand strategy, and campaign production
deep statistical theory beyond applied significance, power, and effect size
data-engineering pipeline implementation beyond the instrumentation contract
pricing strategy and full financial modeling beyond CAC/LTV/ROAS unit economics

glossary.definition: fully-loaded cost to acquire one customer in a defined period and channel
expected discounted margin a customer generates over their lifetime
revenue or value returned per unit of ad spend within a defined window
assignment of conversion credit across marketing touchpoints by a chosen model
the causal lift a marketing action produces versus a no-exposure baseline
a group of customers partitioned by attribute or behavior for targeting
a group defined by shared acquisition or behavioral time of entry tracked over time
an evidence-backed archetype communicating a target segment to teams
the progress a customer seeks in a situation that they hire a product to make
probability a test detects a true effect of a given size at a set alpha

evidence_label_policy.rule: all scores are heuristic priors referencing SRC_HEURISTIC_PRIOR; observed_impact, data_quality, and observed_co_occurrence are 0.0

source_registry.description: model heuristic priors for market-research and marketing-analytics estimates grounded in standard references such as Kotler & Keller Marketing Management and common marketing-analytics practice
source_registry.citation_or_locator: Kotler & Keller, Marketing Management; standard marketing-analytics references
grounding_limits: priors are directional and require validation before decision use

nodes.definition: Translate a business or marketing question into a falsifiable research objective with decisions it will inform, scope, and success criteria.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a downstream decision the research was meant to inform is cancelled or redefined

pros.example: reframe 'do users like the logo' into 'will the rebrand lift activation'
tie survey to go/no-go on a pricing change

cons.example: fixing scope before exploratory interviews hides a churn driver
one survey trying to answer 9 unrelated questions

nodes.definition: Define target population, sampling frame, method (probability vs non-probability), and required sample size so estimates generalize within stated error bounds.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: observed response rate or frame coverage deviates materially from the sampling assumptions

pros.example: probability panel with poststratification weights to census
n=1067 for ±3% at 95% on a proportion

cons.example: mail+phone frame triples fieldwork cost vs river sample
20% response rate skews toward engaged users

nodes.definition: Design questionnaire items, scales, and flow that measure the target constructs with minimal response bias and acceptable completion rates.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a measured construct is redefined or a pilot shows item-level reliability below threshold

pros.example: use a tested NPS+driver battery instead of ad hoc items
cognitive interviews flag a double-barreled question

cons.example: a 40-item grid kills completion on mobile
price question placed after benefit framing inflates WTP

nodes.definition: Plan and conduct in-depth interviews to surface motivations, language, and unmet needs that structured instruments cannot capture.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: thematic saturation is not reached or new segments require fresh recruiting

pros.example: interviewee describes the job they hire the product for
discovers onboarding confusion no survey asked about

cons.example: 8 interviews treated as market-wide proof
interviewer nudges toward a favored feature

nodes.definition: Run moderated group discussions to observe reactions, group dynamics, and concept resonance for early-stage stimuli.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: concept set changes or group composition no longer matches the target audience

pros.example: group debate exposes a polarizing tagline
three groups screen five concepts in a week

cons.example: one vocal participant sways the room
client treats 3 groups as quantitative proof

nodes.definition: Systematically gather and structure competitor, category, and secondary-source data to map the landscape and benchmark position.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a major competitor enters/exits or the category definition shifts

pros.example: secondary teardown reveals an unserved price tier
competitor CAC range frames a realistic goal

cons.example: vendor report uses a different category definition
published pricing omits real discounting

nodes.definition: Specify and validate the event tracking, identifiers, and data pipeline that produce trustworthy behavioral data for analytics.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a deploy or schema change alters event volume or definitions versus the tracking plan

pros.example: a versioned tracking plan keeps CAC and funnel comparable over time
logged-in id links web and app sessions

cons.example: a deploy drops the purchase event and ROAS looks like zero
collecting PII without consent triggers compliance exposure

nodes.definition: Detect and remediate missingness, outliers, bots, duplicates, and bias in collected data before it feeds insight or metrics.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: data distribution or missingness pattern shifts beyond the documented quality thresholds

pros.example: bot traffic removal corrects an inflated conversion rate
an exclusion log lets anyone reconstruct the analysis set

cons.example: trimming 'outliers' removes genuine high-LTV whales
mean-imputing income shifts a segment boundary

nodes.definition: Partition customers into actionable, stable segments using behavioral and attitudinal data to guide targeting and messaging.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: segment stability on a holdout drops or the business changes how it can target

pros.example: a high-intent low-tenure segment gets a tailored onboarding offer
segments replicate on a holdout sample

cons.example: k chosen by aesthetics produces segments no one can target
a 'budget' label suppresses upsell to real upgraders

nodes.definition: Synthesize qualitative and quantitative findings into evidence-backed personas that communicate target customers to teams.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: underlying segmentation or qualitative themes change materially

pros.example: a persona aligns product, marketing, and sales on one target
each persona trait cites a survey or interview source

cons.example: a persona invents a backstory no data supports
nine personas paralyze prioritization

nodes.definition: Model the functional, emotional, and social jobs customers hire products for, with the situations and desired outcomes that drive demand.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new interview evidence reveals a different primary job or switching trigger

pros.example: reveals the real competitor is a spreadsheet, not a rival app
an unmet 'reduce anxiety' outcome guides messaging

cons.example: a 'be successful' job is too broad to act on
prioritization stalls without a sizing study

nodes.definition: Compute fully-loaded cost to acquire a customer by channel and cohort, with consistent cost inclusion and denominator definitions.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: marketing spend categories or channel definitions change versus the CAC definition doc

pros.example: fully loaded CAC kills a channel that looked cheap on media-only cost
CAC creep flags channel saturation early

cons.example: one channel counts salaries, another does not
cheap organic masks an expensive paid channel

nodes.definition: Model expected discounted margin a customer generates over their lifetime, with retention, margin, and horizon assumptions made explicit.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: observed retention or margin deviates from the assumptions feeding the LTV model

pros.example: a 3:1 LTV:CAC threshold gates channel scaling
high-LTV segment justifies a higher allowable CAC

cons.example: fitting a flat tail overstates lifetime by 2x
summing 5 years of margin undiscounted flatters LTV

nodes.definition: Measure revenue or value returned per unit of advertising spend with a defined revenue window, attribution basis, and incrementality caveat.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the attribution model or revenue window underlying ROAS is changed

pros.example: pausing a sub-1 ROAS campaign frees budget for a winner
a fixed 7-day window standardizes reporting

cons.example: high last-click ROAS on brand search is mostly organic demand
a 30-day window over-credits view-through

nodes.definition: Assign credit for conversions across marketing touchpoints using a chosen model, while bounding its causal interpretation.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: touchpoint completeness, privacy signal availability, or the attribution model specification changes

pros.example: upper-funnel display gets credit it was denied by last-click
one shared model removes channel-vs-channel disputes

cons.example: reallocating to high-attribution channels with no real lift
switching to time-decay reorders channel ROAS

nodes.definition: Define funnel stages and measure step conversion and drop-off to locate the highest-leverage points for intervention.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: funnel stage definitions or the underlying events change, breaking rate comparability

pros.example: a 60% drop at checkout prioritizes payment UX
mobile users drop at signup at twice the rate

cons.example: ambiguous 'activated' definition breaks comparability
forcing a linear funnel on a looping journey misleads

nodes.definition: Design controlled online experiments with randomization, a primary metric, and a stopping rule to estimate causal effect of a change.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the primary metric, randomization unit, or stopping rule is changed after launch

pros.example: an A/B test proves a redesign lifts conversion, not seasonality
locking the primary metric stops cherry-picking outcomes

cons.example: stopping when p<0.05 first appears fabricates a win
a test with n too small calls a real effect null

nodes.definition: Apply hypothesis testing, power analysis, and effect-size estimation to decide whether an observed difference is real and meaningful; composes the statistics specialist.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the test family, alpha/power targets, or effect-size priors driving inference change

pros.example: a CI that crosses zero halts a premature rollout
an MDE calc sets the sample needed for a 2% lift

cons.example: testing 20 metrics yields a spurious 'winner'
a significant 0.1% lift is not worth shipping

nodes.definition: Group users by acquisition or behavioral cohort and track retention and value over time to separate lifecycle effects from mix shifts.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: cohort definition or acquisition mix changes enough to alter retention interpretation

pros.example: a falling blended rate is just a big low-quality cohort
cohort triangles ground the LTV retention assumption

cons.example: a 2-week cohort's 'great' retention reverses
switching from signup to first-purchase cohort flips trends

nodes.definition: Integrate quantitative and qualitative findings into prioritized, decision-linked recommendations with explicit confidence and caveats.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new or contradicting evidence arrives, or the decision the report informs changes

pros.example: one ranked recommendation set replaces ten disconnected charts
labeling a finding 'directional' avoids a costly bet

cons.example: a clean story drops the contradicting data
reporting before the key test returns misleads the decision

nodes.definition: Maintain a governed catalog of metric definitions, owners, and dashboards so reported numbers stay consistent, trusted, and comparable over time.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a key metric definition changes or a new dashboard becomes a decision source

pros.example: CAC means the same thing in every deck and dashboard
a definition change is dated so historical trends stay honest

cons.example: heavy approval gates delay a needed metric tweak
an out-of-date definition silently misleads

edges.resolution_rule: objective dominates; resize sample when objective changes

edges.why_related: questionnaire constructs come from the objective
edges.risk_of_conflict: items without an objective measure nothing actionable
edges.example: objective defines the constructs the survey must measure

edges.why_related: what to track is determined by the decisions the research informs
edges.risk_of_conflict: tracking everything or nothing without a question
edges.example: objective sets which behavioral events are decision-relevant
edges.resolution_rule: objective dominates the tracking plan scope

edges.why_related: competitor scope is bounded by the strategic question
edges.example: objective selects the relevant competitive set

edges.why_related: quality checks run on instrumented event streams
edges.risk_of_conflict: cleaning data that was never validly collected
edges.example: instrumentation produces the stream that quality processes clean

edges.why_related: nonresponse and weighting feed survey data quality
edges.example: sampling plan defines weighting that quality must apply

edges.why_related: segmentation requires cleaned, deduplicated data
edges.example: clean data is prerequisite to valid clusters

edges.why_related: ltv modeling needs clean retention and margin data
edges.example: data quality bounds the validity of LTV inputs

edges.why_related: cohorts must be built on clean, deduplicated events
edges.example: clean data is prerequisite to cohort retention

edges.why_related: cac denominators come from validated acquisition events
edges.example: instrumentation supplies the acquisition events CAC counts

edges.why_related: cac requires clean spend and conversion data
edges.example: clean data bounds CAC accuracy

edges.why_related: attribution needs validated touchpoint paths
edges.example: instrumentation supplies the touchpoint data attribution models

edges.why_related: attribution paths must be cleaned and deduplicated
edges.example: clean data bounds attribution validity

edges.why_related: roas revenue credit depends on the attribution model
edges.example: attribution assigns the revenue ROAS divides by spend

edges.why_related: roas needs validated revenue and spend events
edges.example: instrumentation supplies revenue events ROAS uses

edges.why_related: funnel stages map to instrumented events
edges.example: instrumentation defines the events funnel stages count

edges.why_related: funnel rates require clean event data
edges.example: clean data bounds funnel rate validity

edges.why_related: funnel diagnosis identifies what to test
edges.example: funnel locates the drop-off an experiment should target

edges.why_related: experiments need reliable metric instrumentation
edges.example: instrumentation supplies the primary metric an experiment reads

edges.why_related: significance testing consumes experiment design and data
edges.example: experiment supplies the data and design significance tests evaluate
edges.resolution_rule: experiment design dominates the test it enables

edges.why_related: survey length and mode interact with sampling mode
edges.risk_of_conflict: instrument that the frame cannot deliver
edges.example: sampling mode constrains feasible survey design
edges.resolution_rule: coordinate; sampling mode bounds survey length

edges.why_related: jtbd job maps are built from interview evidence
edges.example: interviews supply the switching stories JTBD codes

edges.why_related: personas draw qualitative texture from interviews
edges.example: interviews supply the qualitative attributes personas use

edges.why_related: personas are anchored to data-driven segments
edges.example: segmentation supplies the quantitative backbone of personas

edges.why_related: segment-level ltv requires segment definitions
edges.example: segments define the groups LTV is computed within

edges.why_related: observed cohort retention curves drive ltv extrapolation
edges.example: cohort retention changes the LTV horizon estimate
edges.resolution_rule: use cohort curves as LTV retention input

edges.why_related: ltv must exceed cac for sustainable growth
edges.example: CAC bounds the acquisition spend LTV can justify

edges.why_related: channel cac allocation depends on attribution credit
edges.risk_of_conflict: cac credited to the wrong channel
edges.example: attribution decides which channel a conversion's cost lands on
edges.resolution_rule: shared attribution model bounds CAC channeling

edges.why_related: synthesis must wait for significance verdicts on key tests
edges.example: significance verdicts gate which findings enter the report

edges.why_related: recommendations on spend rely on cac
edges.example: CAC outputs feed acquisition recommendations

edges.why_related: value recommendations rely on ltv
edges.example: LTV outputs feed value and targeting recommendations

edges.why_related: competitive context frames recommendations
edges.example: competitive findings contextualize the synthesis

edges.why_related: roas disputes trigger metric definition governance
edges.example: roas inconsistency signals a definition needing governance; stop when one owned definition is certified
edges.resolution_rule: governance owns the canonical definition; stop when certified

edges.why_related: cac definition disputes route to governance
edges.risk_of_conflict: cac means different things per team
edges.example: CAC inconsistency triggers a governance change; stop when one definition is owned and dated
edges.resolution_rule: governance owns CAC definition; stop at certified catalog entry

edges.why_related: findings can reopen or refine the original objective
edges.example: synthesis can reveal the objective was mis-framed; stop after one re-scope per cycle
edges.resolution_rule: re-scope at most once per research cycle, then proceed

edges.why_related: funnel stage metrics must conform to governed definitions
edges.example: governance constrains how funnel stages are defined

edges.why_related: attributed credit competes with experimental incrementality as the basis of truth
edges.risk_of_conflict: shipping on attribution that an experiment would refute
edges.example: high-attribution channel shows no lift in a holdout test
edges.resolution_rule: when they disagree, experimental incrementality dominates attribution for causal claims

edges.why_related: experiment velocity competes with waiting for clean funnel baselines
edges.risk_of_conflict: testing before the funnel is understood
edges.example: team A/B tests a step before its drop-off is even measured
edges.resolution_rule: baseline the funnel step first unless cost of delay is high

edges.why_related: thorough cleaning competes with deadline-driven synthesis
edges.example: a deadline pushes synthesis before bot filtering completes
edges.resolution_rule: data-quality gate dominates; no synthesis on uncleaned data

edges.why_related: richer instruments raise burden, hurting response and sample quality
edges.risk_of_conflict: long survey that wrecks response rate
edges.example: adding a 20-item battery drops completion below the sampling assumption
edges.resolution_rule: cap instrument length to protect the sampling plan

conflict_axes.trigger: a decision deadline arrives before rigorous data collection completes
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: for irreversible or high-spend decisions rigor dominates; for cheap reversible bets speed may dominate with explicit caveats
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: decision is irreversible and evidence is below the minimum bar
conflict_axes.example: ship a rebrand on 3 focus groups vs wait for a powered survey

conflict_axes.trigger: an attribution model and an incrementality test disagree on a channel's value
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: experimental incrementality dominates attribution whenever a causal spend decision is at stake
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a budget shift above threshold relies on attributed-only ROAS
conflict_axes.example: brand-search last-click ROAS is high but a holdout shows near-zero lift

conflict_axes.trigger: a small-n qualitative finding is presented as a market-wide fact
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: qualitative informs hypotheses; quantitative validates generalization; neither is dropped
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a qualitative-only claim drives a company-wide bet
conflict_axes.example: 8 interviews used to justify a market-sizing claim

conflict_axes.trigger: an analyst needs a new metric faster than governance can certify it
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: ad-hoc metrics permitted for exploration but governed definitions dominate any decision or external report
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: an uncertified metric is used in a board deck
conflict_axes.example: two teams report different CAC in the same meeting

conflict_axes.trigger: richer tracking is proposed that increases privacy and consent exposure
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: privacy and consent constraints dominate tracking breadth; collect only decision-relevant, consented data
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: collecting PII without a lawful basis or consent
conflict_axes.example: tracking a sensitive attribute with no consent flow

conflict_axes.trigger: the best-fitting clusters are not targetable or sized for action
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: actionability and stability dominate marginal statistical fit when choosing the segmentation
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a chosen scheme cannot be operationalized in any channel
conflict_axes.example: an elegant cluster maps to no addressable audience

conflict_axes.trigger: retention extrapolation assumptions materially change the LTV:CAC verdict
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: conservative LTV assumptions dominate when an optimistic curve is the only thing making acquisition look profitable
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: spend scaling depends on an unvalidated flat retention tail
conflict_axes.example: optimistic LTV flips a channel from unprofitable to profitable

conflict_axes.trigger: a statistically significant effect is too small to matter or a real effect is underpowered
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: practical effect size dominates bare p-values; ship only effects above the minimum meaningful threshold
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a 0.1% significant lift is treated as a win
conflict_axes.example: a meaningful lift is dismissed because an underpowered test was null

conflict_axes.trigger: exploratory evidence suggests the original objective was mis-framed
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: objective stability dominates to prevent endless drift, but one evidence-driven re-scope per cycle is allowed
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: every new interview reopens the entire research scope
conflict_axes.example: a churn driver emerges that the fixed objective excluded

edge_cases.trigger: a deploy renames or drops a tracked event
edge_cases.failure_mode: downstream metrics silently shift or zero out
edge_cases.example: purchase event renamed, ROAS drops to zero overnight
edge_cases.detection_method: monitor event volume against a tracking-plan baseline with anomaly alerts

edge_cases.trigger: attributed ROAS is used to justify a causal budget shift
edge_cases.failure_mode: spend moved to a channel with no real incremental lift
edge_cases.example: high last-click ROAS channel fails a geo holdout
edge_cases.detection_method: cross-check attribution against an incrementality experiment before reallocation

edge_cases.trigger: small-n qualitative findings are reported as market-wide facts
edge_cases.failure_mode: over-generalized claim drives a wrong company bet
edge_cases.example: 8 interviews cited as proof of total addressable demand
edge_cases.detection_method: check that generalizing claims trace to a quantitative sample

edge_cases.trigger: an experiment is stopped when p<0.05 first appears
edge_cases.failure_mode: inflated false-positive rate fabricates a win
edge_cases.example: test halted at first significant peek without correction
edge_cases.detection_method: compare stopping time to the predeclared rule; check for sequential peeking

edge_cases.trigger: retention is extrapolated with an over-optimistic flat tail
edge_cases.failure_mode: LTV inflated, unprofitable acquisition looks viable
edge_cases.detection_method: validate retention curve against mature holdout cohorts and sensitivity band

edge_cases.trigger: channels use different cost-inclusion or attribution rules
edge_cases.failure_mode: CAC is not comparable across channels and misallocates budget
edge_cases.example: one channel counts headcount, another does not
edge_cases.detection_method: reconcile CAC to finance spend and a single shared definition

edge_cases.trigger: low response or frame gaps make the sample unrepresentative
edge_cases.failure_mode: biased estimates generalized to the population
edge_cases.example: 20% response rate skewed to power users
edge_cases.detection_method: compare respondent profile to known population and check weighting

edge_cases.trigger: clusters do not replicate on a holdout sample
edge_cases.failure_mode: unstable segments and personas chase noise
edge_cases.example: k chosen on training data collapses on holdout
edge_cases.detection_method: require segment replication on a holdout before use

edge_cases.trigger: funnel stage definitions change without versioning
edge_cases.failure_mode: conversion trends become incomparable over time
edge_cases.detection_method: diff current stage definitions against the governed catalog version

edge_cases.trigger: many metrics are tested without correction
edge_cases.failure_mode: a spurious significant 'winner' emerges by chance
edge_cases.example: 20 secondary metrics surface a fake lift
edge_cases.detection_method: count tested hypotheses and verify multiplicity correction applied

edge_cases.trigger: stale or mis-defined secondary data is treated as current truth
edge_cases.example: a two-year-old market-size figure quoted as current
edge_cases.detection_method: require dated citation and category-definition check on each secondary figure

workflow.objective: frame the decision-linked research objective and success criteria
workflow.do_first_because: objective drives every method, sample, and metric choice; mis-scoping causes total rework

workflow.objective: design sampling, instruments, and tracking before any collection
workflow.do_first_because: fixing collection design before fielding prevents un-recoverable data defects

workflow.objective: collect primary and secondary data per the design
workflow.do_first_because: collection must follow a locked design or the data cannot be trusted later

workflow.objective: clean, deduplicate, and validate data and document exclusions
workflow.do_first_because: every downstream metric and model inherits data-quality defects, so clean before analyzing

workflow.objective: derive segments, jobs, personas, and cohorts from clean data
workflow.do_first_because: customer-insight models feed targeting and metric segmentation and must rest on clean data

workflow.objective: compute acquisition, value, efficiency, and funnel metrics
workflow.do_first_because: metrics depend on clean data and a fixed attribution basis to be comparable

workflow.objective: design and evaluate controlled experiments on high-leverage funnel steps
workflow.do_first_because: predeclaring metric, power, and stopping rule before running prevents p-hacking rework

workflow.objective: integrate findings into prioritized, confidence-labeled recommendations
workflow.do_first_because: synthesis must wait for significant verdicts and reconciled metrics to avoid reporting noise

workflow.objective: certify metric definitions and dashboards used for ongoing decisions
workflow.do_first_because: governed definitions prevent dueling numbers and keep future reporting comparable

workflow.objective: capture follow-up questions and update objectives for the next cycle
workflow.do_first_because: structured iteration converts findings into the next objective without endless re-scoping

feeds personas, LTV, and metric segmentation

communicates segments to teams once grounded

value side of sustainable acquisition

dominance_rules.trigger: high-risk or irreversible decision under deadline pressure
dominance_rules.rule: risk and irreversibility dominate speed for high-stakes decisions
dominance_rules.required_action: hold the decision until the minimum evidence bar is met
dominance_rules.example: do not greenlight an irreversible rebrand on underpowered evidence

dominance_rules.trigger: attribution and an incrementality test disagree
dominance_rules.rule: experimental incrementality dominates attribution for causal spend claims
dominance_rules.required_action: require a holdout/geo test before large reallocation
dominance_rules.example: a holdout overrides a flattering last-click ROAS

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-value node depends on an unfinished prerequisite
dominance_rules.rule: dependency order dominates raw value ordering
dominance_rules.required_action: sequence prerequisites before dependents regardless of value
dominance_rules.example: do not compute ROAS before the attribution model exists

dominance_rules.trigger: a precise number rests on a weak evidence label
dominance_rules.rule: evidence-label correctness dominates apparent numeric precision
dominance_rules.required_action: downgrade unsupported precision to its true confidence
dominance_rules.example: a 2-decimal CAC from a tiny sample is reported with its uncertainty

dominance_rules.trigger: a deadline pushes synthesis before cleaning finishes
dominance_rules.required_action: block synthesis until the quality gate passes
dominance_rules.example: no recommendation issued on un-bot-filtered conversion data

dominance_rules.trigger: a significant effect is trivially small or a real effect is underpowered
dominance_rules.rule: practical effect size dominates bare statistical significance
dominance_rules.required_action: compare effect to the minimum meaningful threshold before acting
dominance_rules.example: a significant 0.1% lift is not shipped

dominance_rules.rule: privacy and consent dominate data-capture breadth
dominance_rules.example: drop a sensitive attribute that lacks a consent flow

dominance_rules.trigger: an uncertified metric is proposed for a decision or external report
dominance_rules.rule: governed metric definitions dominate ad-hoc metrics for any decision use
dominance_rules.required_action: require certification before decision or external use
dominance_rules.example: a board-deck CAC must use the certified definition

dominance_rules.trigger: risk, irreversibility, or low confidence crosses review thresholds
dominance_rules.rule: human review dominates automation past risk/confidence thresholds
dominance_rules.required_action: route to a reviewer before locking the decision
dominance_rules.example: a high-risk attribution change is human-reviewed before adoption

dominance_rules.trigger: pressure to add many metrics threatens definition stability
dominance_rules.rule: metric-definition stability dominates raw metric volume
dominance_rules.required_action: add metrics only with an owned, versioned definition

anti_rework_rules.rule: do not collect data before the objective and decision linkage are locked
anti_rework_rules.rationale: collection without a decision-linked objective produces unusable data
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: fieldwork started with no approved brief
anti_rework_rules.example: a survey is fielded then found to answer no decision

anti_rework_rules.rule: do not field instruments or tracking before sampling and instrument design pass review
anti_rework_rules.rationale: design defects in collection are unrecoverable after fielding
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: data collected before pilot or tracking plan review
anti_rework_rules.example: an un-piloted item produces uninterpretable responses

anti_rework_rules.rule: do not compute metrics before the tracking plan is versioned and validated
anti_rework_rules.rationale: metrics on unvalidated events are silently wrong
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: CAC/ROAS reported with no tracking-plan baseline
anti_rework_rules.example: ROAS reads zero because an event was renamed

anti_rework_rules.rule: do not segment, model LTV, or build cohorts before the data-quality gate passes
anti_rework_rules.rationale: models inherit and amplify data defects
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: clustering or LTV run on uncleaned data
anti_rework_rules.example: segments built on bot-inflated events collapse later

anti_rework_rules.rule: do not finalize ROAS or channel CAC before the attribution model is fixed
anti_rework_rules.rationale: switching attribution later reorders all channel results
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: ROAS published before an attribution basis is chosen
anti_rework_rules.example: a model change reshuffles channel winners post-decision

anti_rework_rules.rule: do not run experiments before the target funnel step is baselined
anti_rework_rules.rationale: testing without a baseline wastes traffic on low-leverage steps
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: an A/B test launched on an unmeasured step
anti_rework_rules.example: testing a step with negligible drop-off

anti_rework_rules.rule: do not start an experiment before predeclaring metric, power, and stopping rule
anti_rework_rules.rationale: post-hoc metric choice and peeking fabricate significance
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: no predeclared primary metric on record
anti_rework_rules.example: a winner is picked from many post-hoc metrics

anti_rework_rules.rule: do not synthesize confident recommendations before significance verdicts on key tests
anti_rework_rules.rationale: reporting noise as a finding misleads decisions
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a recommendation cites an unconcluded test
anti_rework_rules.example: a directional lift is reported as proven

anti_rework_rules.rule: do not certify the metric catalog before metrics reconcile to source/finance
anti_rework_rules.rationale: governing wrong definitions locks in errors
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: catalog certified while CAC fails finance reconciliation
anti_rework_rules.example: a certified metric still disputes finance numbers

anti_rework_rules.rule: do not re-open the objective more than once per research cycle
anti_rework_rules.rationale: unbounded re-scoping prevents the research from ever concluding
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: more than one scope change recorded in a cycle
anti_rework_rules.example: every new finding reopens the entire scope

iteration_protocol.trigger: a validation or quality check fails
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: no open failures above materiality threshold

iteration_protocol.detection: rank by risk_score and downstream coupling
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: queue empty or only sub-threshold defects remain

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect touches a high-coupling node
iteration_protocol.detection: trace dependency and edge fan-out from the node
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: impact map stable across two passes

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect is queued for repair
iteration_protocol.detection: map failure type to owning subsystem
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: no queued defect lacks an owner

iteration_protocol.trigger: a repair modifies a locked or high-coupling component
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: validation passes with no new failures

iteration_protocol.trigger: new evidence shifts a node's importance beyond the revisit delta
risk, irreversibility, or low confidence crosses a threshold
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: human decision recorded for the flagged item

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new KB or model version is produced
iteration_protocol.detection: compare metrics and counts to the prior version

test_cases.input_summary: objective-only research request with no data
attribution and incrementality disagree on a channel
CAC and ROAS reported across teams
expected_properties: feedback edges route disputes to governance

version_increment_rules: increment on any hard-locked metric definition change
lock_downgrade_rules: downgrade hard_lock to soft_lock when a governed definition is contested with evidence
